entities.name: Kyaw Soe Oo
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Kyaw Soe Oo, born around 1990, emerged as a prominent Burmese journalist and media personality in the early 21st century, gaining international recognition primarily through his work with Reuters and People Media. His career became emblematic of the precarious state of press freedom in Myanmar, particularly following the 2017 crackdown on Rohingya Muslims in Rakhine State. His investigative reporting, often conducted under challenging and dangerous conditions, brought critical attention to human rights abuses and state violence, making him a significant figure in contemporary Burmese journalism and a symbol for global media advocacy.

His most notable work includes his involvement in a Reuters investigation into the Inn Din massacre, a mass killing of Rohingya men by the Myanmar military and local Rakhine Buddhists in September 2017. Alongside his colleague Wa Lone, Kyaw Soe Oo was arrested on December 12, 2017, under the colonial-era Official Secrets Act, after being handed classified documents by police officers. Their subsequent trial and conviction in September 2018, which led to seven-year prison sentences, sparked widespread international condemnation from governments, human rights organizations, and press freedom advocates, highlighting the severe restrictions on independent reporting in Myanmar.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Kyaw Soe Oo's case became a global symbol for press freedom, drawing international attention to the plight of journalists in authoritarian regimes and contributing to the documentation of the Rohingya genocide. His work directly led to a Pulitzer Prize and influenced diplomatic pressure on Myanmar.
